title: Trading Sessions & Market Hours
hook: Different sessions, different behavior. Know which one you're looking at.

launchpad.outcome: Weigh a chart move differently depending on which session it formed in.
launchpad.missionQuestion: Does a break of structure mean the same thing overnight on thin volume as it does at the New York open?

slides.headline: Same chart. Different hours.
slides.line: The same chart behaves differently depending on what time it is.

cards.label: Asia
cards.sub: Tends to be quiet and range-bound.

cards.label: London
cards.sub: Often brings the first real expansion of the day.

cards.label: New York (RTH open)
cards.sub: Usually the highest volume and sharpest moves.

cards.label: Not “better”
cards.sub: Just different. Same setup, different session, different look.

slides.headline: Know the clock.
slides.line: Every session in Eastern and Pacific time. Find yours.

schedule.note: London and NY AM overlap from 9:30 AM to 12:00 PM ET (6:30 to 9:00 AM PT). ET stays the same all year: EST in winter, EDT in summer.

check.prompt: It’s 11:00 AM Pacific. Which session are you in?

options.label: London
options.feedback: London wraps up at 9:00 AM Pacific. Check the clock again.

options.label: NY Lunch
options.feedback: NY Lunch runs 9:00 to 10:30 AM Pacific. 11:00 is just after it.

options.label: NY PM
options.why: NY PM runs 10:30 AM to 1:00 PM Pacific (1:30 to 4:00 PM Eastern).

slides.headline: Same level. Two tests.
slides.line: Tested overnight on thin volume. Retested at the New York open on much higher volume.

options.label: They’re equal
options.feedback: Volume differences between sessions are real information, not noise to ignore.

options.label: The New York open retest
options.why: Right. More real participants means the reaction reflects more genuine agreement or disagreement.

slides.headline: New York lines up with US stock hours.

check.prompt: The New York session (RTH open) typically brings the highest ___ and sharpest moves.

options.label: Spread
options.feedback: Spread isn’t what defines a session’s character. Participation is.

options.label: Fees
options.feedback: Fees don’t change session to session. Volume and participation do.

options.label: Volume
options.why: It overlaps with US stock market hours and major news, driving the most participation.

slides.quote: A level in London and a level at the New York open don’t carry the same weight.
slides.line: I’m not telling you to only trade one session. I’m telling you to know which session you’re looking at.

slides.prompt: Why does it matter what time a breakout happens?
slides.modelAnswer: The same-looking break of structure means different things depending on how many real participants were actually there to make it happen. A break on thin overnight volume can look identical to one at the New York open, but the New York version reflects way more real conviction, ignoring session context throws away free information the chart is already giving you.

takeaways: Asia, London, and New York each behave differently, none is "better," just different.
A move on heavy volume carries more real information than the same-looking move on thin volume.
Ignoring session context throws away free, useful information.
remember: A level in London and a level at the New York open don't carry the same weight.
